title: web-server
intention: A thin web presentation surface (Law 7) over the running system: the devices on the heartbeat across the top, and the selected device's ACTIVE page below — a stack of standard PANES (STATUS / INTERACTION / SETTINGS / LOGGING; names are placeholders, final labels must read to an averageish human). The panes are STANDARD MACHINERY in BaseShim, not in each device and not in the web server: a device fills a pane by providing a handler, and declares WHICH panes it offers (STATUS + SETTINGS are the guaranteed floor via Form v0 #2; INTERACTION/LOGGING/future are declared, and a device may declare more than one of a kind — the librarian's chat-page + tool-page fall out as two declared interaction surfaces, not a special case). A pane with no handler renders empty/absent. The web server itself is a dumb HTTP<->bus bridge + frame renderer; it owns NO device state.
why: Telos 2 — the librarian needs a web interface, and 'a web interface falls out of the chatbot' only if the surface exists first; this is that surface, on the spine before the librarian. It is the Form v0 #2 introspection surface (MAP.md:157) MADE CONCRETE — the SAME protocol the tester probes and the web UI renders, so observability is not a separate build (STATUS = intention+why+state; SETTINGS = settings; INTERACTION = the reserved `other` channel). Reported-vs-filed intention on the STATUS pane is a live drift detector (Law 3). Building it as a presentation surface (Law 7: may collapse an error into a coherent shape; never a record of truth) keeps the intelligence in the shims and the web server trivial (minimalism; one owner, no state).
traces_to: Telos 2 (Cairn has a USER — the librarian's web interface rests on this surface)
Form v0 #2 (MAP.md:157 — the uniform introspection surface; one protocol for tester + web UI)
Law 7 (a presentation surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape; a record of truth never may)
Law 6 (the web server owns no state — content is each device's, reached through its gate; a kill travels the bus to the OWNER, the shim, which runs it — the web server only describes the command)
Law 4 (gates not supervisors; the circuit breaker halts by physics — cgroup-kill — not by asking a runaway to stop)
build order: web server, after inference domain (MAP.md:888)

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate (tester) — the tester runs each child's proof and emits a VALIDATION, verdict+seal from the same hand. THIS SESSION'S LESSON, made a gate: the VALIDATION must be PERSISTED via db_domain (store.persist_validation) and grep back — a produced-but-unpersisted validation did NOT happen (the exact miss that bit inference_domain, 2026-07-21). Durability gate (code-seam): not done until proven, VALIDATION persisted, AND committed (git). Kicks back on red proof -> design/build at the point of creation (CP2).
falsifier.proves_red: the surface is honest and thin: a device's ACTIVE page shows exactly the panes it DECLARES (no more, no less); STATUS shows reported-vs-filed intention and flags drift when they differ; the web server holds NO device state of its own (everything rendered is pulled live from the device's shim over the bus, from disk intentions, or from db_domain reads). Wrong-shape signals: (1) if presentation logic migrates INTO the shims (shims emitting HTML instead of surface DATA), the tester can no longer probe the same protocol — the data/render split has failed; (2) if the web server accretes its own state/cache of device internals, it has stopped being a presentation surface and become a second record of truth (Law 7 breach); (3) if the standard panes stop being standard (each device re-implementing its own STATUS), BaseShim was the wrong home.
falsifier.horizon: first real render — when the web server shows at least two live devices' ACTIVE pages pulled over the bus, STATUS drift-detection works, and the LOGGING pane reads real emission. Re-check then: is BaseShim the right home for the standard machinery, or do too many devices override it? And revisit the data/render split the first time an INTERACTION surface needs a rich device-provided view (the librarian's tool page) — standard panes = data + generic render, interaction panes = may bring their own template.

children: (BUILT + PROVEN + PERSISTED 2026-07-22, cairn) a — the standard surface machinery in BaseShim: a device DECLARES its panes and provides handlers; BaseShim assembles the ACTIVE payload as structured DATA (extending introspect(): intention/state/settings/other -> the pane set). Surfaces are a declared LIST, not a fixed enum; STATUS+SETTINGS are the floor, the rest declared, multiples allowed. LANDED: BaseDevice.declared_panes() (default [], the offered extras with handlers) + BaseShim.active_page() (the standard assembly — STATUS+SETTINGS projected from introspect(), declared panes appended in order, multiples allowed, an unwired or raising handler renders ABSENT-with-reason not fatal (CP2/Law 7), the whole page json-round-trips so it is DATA not HTML). Proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_active_page.py (5 teeth), green under the tester, VALIDATION persisted beside-code at cairn/tools/base/validations/test_active_page.json. FILED EDGE: STATUS carries only the REPORTED intention; the reported-vs-filed DRIFT comparison is child b's render-time job (it reads disk intentions), not the shim's.

(BUILT + PROVEN + PERSISTED 2026-07-22, cairn) b — the web_server device: a standing daemon (launched via launchers/, instance at ~/.cairn/devices/web_server/0/), owning its listening PORT (Law 6). A dumb HTTP<->bus bridge: browser <-> HTTP <-> web_server <-> bus <-> each device's shim. Renders the standard panes' DATA to HTML (interaction panes may bring their own view). v0: bind LOCALHOST, single operator (Akien) — it exposes device internals and (later) a kill switch. Python stdlib http.server; no framework unless a real need pulls one. LANDED: cairn/devices/web_server/ — render.py (pure data->html, everything a device says HTML-escaped), server.py (WebServerDevice.serve(path)->(status,ctype,html), reaching each device's active_page live THROUGH the ground_loop that beats it — in-process v0, the bus request/reply transport FILED), daemon.py (the thin http.server localhost wrapper, smoke-tested binding+serving, kept out of the proof as the unprovable-without-OS piece). Proof test_web_server.py (6 teeth: nav-is-roster, panes render, coherent-404-still-shows-nav, device-strings-escaped, absent-pane-reason, owns-no-state), green under the tester, VALIDATION at cairn/devices/web_server/validations/test_web_server.json. ground_loop gained shim_for(id) (a read accessor — reach a device THROUGH the heartbeat that holds it). Charter cairn/devices/web_server/intention+why.json. Filed edges carried: the bus transport, reported-vs-filed drift on STATUS, rich interaction views, and the launcher wiring the REAL running heartbeat (daemon.py stubs an empty one today).

(BUILT + PROVEN + PERSISTED 2026-07-22, cairn) c — ground_loop contracted to publish the live heartbeat ROSTER (the devices it beats to) at all times; that roster IS the nav across the top. Extends the heartbeat's existing knowledge of its subscribers — no new owner. LANDED: GroundLoopDevice.roster() returns {beats, devices:[{device, awake}]} — the subscription list in order, each with live wakefulness (its shim's running), published at all times (before the first beat too); a device absent from subscriptions is absent from the nav; DATA the web server renders. Proven as a tooth in cairn/devices/ground_loop/proofs/test_ground_loop.py, green under the tester, VALIDATION persisted beside-code at cairn/devices/ground_loop/validations/test_ground_loop.json. No new owner — it is the subscription list ground_loop already owns (Law 6).

(BUILT + PROVEN + PERSISTED 2026-07-24, cairn) d — the VOYAGE pane / ⚓ Harbor route: renders harbor_master's TRAFFIC IMAGE (harbor-master child c) — the whole-fleet, state-right-now view — as a fleet-wide route, distinct from the per-device pages. LANDED: render.render_traffic_image (pure data->html, calm-when-healthy: each emergent gate's underway COUNT + its flagged boats as readable lines, every boat-derived string escaped) + the /harbor route in server.serve (harbor source INJECTED, not imported — the data/render split holds; a surface with none says so with a coherent 404) + the ⚓ Harbor link in render_nav on every page. Proof cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_voyage_pane.py (4 teeth, sealed under a real netns), VALIDATION beside-code. This cashes out the map's Events-vs-Voyages split's Voyages side (cross-device/fleet), rendered from harbor_master, the device that owns the register+voyages (the 'artifact-owner' this waited on, now real). Because the traffic image is disk-computed, /harbor renders the REAL fleet from a bare daemon TODAY — the first live human-visible Cairn surface (Telos 2). The LOGGING pane (per-device Events) remains a later surface; a device may still declare its own ticket view via the same machinery.

(deferred, waits on the cgroup-kill sudo script) e — the SETTINGS pane's CIRCUIT BREAKER: the web server presents the button; the halt travels the bus to the device's shim, which kills the device's cgroup subtree (cgroup v2 cgroup.kill — inescapable by forking/re-parenting, the likely cause of past failed kills) via a narrow least-privilege sudo script (sudo-relay pattern). Presentation describes; the owner runs; the kill is physics (Law 4).
